title: What Job Sharing Platforms 2.0 Is
definition: Job Sharing Platforms 2.0: next-gen platforms splitting jobs.
description:
Job Sharing Platforms 2.0: next-gen platforms splitting jobs. This is Future Education & Work at its most ambitious — split contracts research, platform logistics engineering and handoff tools operations converging on a single goal: making platform hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Education & Work will decide benefit sharing outcomes this century. Job Sharing Platforms 2.0 is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working platform hulls, the larger split contracts vision stalls, and with it, the platform logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Job Sharing Platforms 2.0 in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

definition: Today's documented research behind Job Sharing Platforms 2.0.

title: 2030 — First platform hulls networks graduate 100
definition: 2030 milestone on the Job Sharing Platforms 2.0 roadmap.
description:
First platform hulls networks graduate 100,000 learners with handoff tools credentials employers trust.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed split contracts demonstrations, platform logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting handoff tools uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Job Sharing Platforms 2.0
definition: Estimates Job Sharing Platforms 2.0 readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Job Sharing Platforms 2.0 components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a platform hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

definition: Simulates Job Sharing Platforms 2.0 operating for a day.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where split contracts monitoring, platform logistics redundancy, or handoff tools maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Job Sharing Platforms 2.0 Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Job Sharing Platforms 2.0: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Job Sharing Platforms 2.0 — next-gen platforms splitting jobs.

Phase 1 — Prove (split contracts): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (platform logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (handoff tools): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (benefit sharing): platform hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and workers-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
